title: My AI agents found an unmapped Maya site?
lede: A software engineer set 48 AI agents on public NASA lidar of the Maya lowlands and found a hilltop civic centre missing from Mexico's site register, though archaeologists had already mapped it in 2025.

points: The agents turned about 1,200 square kilometres of lidar strips into images and inspected them one by one against a written guide, with no custom classifier.
They flagged a levelled plaza, an oval pyramid at least 8 m tall, a raised courtyard and a possible rainwater reservoir.
The author sent a Spanish report to INAH, which replied within a day that the location had no registered site.
An update says the site appears in a 2025 study by Estrada-Belli and colleagues, which the agents missed in their literature search.

points.text: Several commenters say the result shows why agent output needs checking, since the 'unmapped' site was already in a published paper.
The author joined the thread to confirm the earlier 2025 paper and say both the agents and the author missed it.
Some want an archaeologist's verification before accepting what the structures are, and doubt the fast official reply means much.
Others note that finding sites is now easier than excavating and protecting them from looters.
A maker of a public UK lidar map says hobbyists already report new sites with such tools almost weekly.
